title: This Artist Turns Pumpkins into Spooky Sculptures
summary:
Looking for Halloween pumpkin ideas? Artist Ray Villafane does not just carve pumpkins. He turns them into detailed 3-D sculptures, usually with spooky faces.

Villafane was born in Queens, New York, and grew up on Long Island. After art school, he moved to Michigan and became an art teacher. One Halloween, he sculpted a pumpkin that impressed his students so much that they asked him to make more. Soon, local hotels and restaurants wanted his pumpkins too.

"I really enjoyed what I had stumbled upon," Villafane says.

His skills led to jobs making toys. In 2006, he started part-time at Marvel Comics, where his wax sculpture of Wolverine from X-Men was turned into a real product. He later worked full-time at DC Comics. But pumpkins remained his true love, and in 2010 he left to carve them full-time. He has also won Food Network's Outrageous Pumpkins competition twice and makes sculptures from sand, sticks and wood.

One of his permanent works is the "Boneyard Mining Company" at Vulture City Ghost Town in Arizona. It tells the story of two creatures: Gordy, who dreams big, and Grimgor, who doubts everything. Villafane says they represent the optimist and pessimist inside all of us.

This Halloween, Villafane's work is on display at the Great Gilbert Gourd Hunt in Gilbert, Arizona, through November 1, 2026. It features more than 40 pumpkin characters set up in scenes around the town. On October 24, visitors can watch him carve a pumpkin live.

His top tip? Pick a big, heavy pumpkin with plenty to carve, and don't worry if it isn't perfectly round. Odd shapes add character.
why_it_matters: Villafane's story shows how a classroom hobby can grow into a career, and how art can bring a whole community together during a holiday.

keywords.explanation: Sculptures are works of art made by carving, shaping or building materials into 3-D forms.
3-D means three-dimensional, having height, width and depth instead of being flat.
An optimist is a person who expects good things to happen.
A pessimist is a person who expects things to go badly.
Permanent means meant to last for a long time without being taken away.

background_read: Carving pumpkins into jack-o'-lanterns is a popular Halloween tradition in the United States.
Most people cut simple shapes through a pumpkin's shell, but sculptors like Villafane carve the thick flesh into detailed 3-D faces and figures.
Sculpting skills can carry over to other jobs, such as designing toys and action figures, as they did for Villafane.
Towns often hold fall displays where artists set up pumpkin scenes for visitors to explore.
